name: Doxa
tagline: The orange-dial dive watch pioneer since 1967
summary: Doxa is a Swiss watchmaker founded in 1889 whose SUB 300 of 1967 was one of the first professional dive watches offered to the public. Famous for its orange dials, cushion cases and no-decompression bezel, it remains a cult favourite among divers and tool-watch fans at accessible prices.
history:
Doxa was founded in 1889 in Le Locle by 21-year-old Georges Ducommun. The name, Greek for 'glory', gained recognition when an anti-magnetic Doxa pocket watch won a gold medal at the 1906 Milan World's Fair, and in 1907 the brand patented an eight-day movement that later equipped dashboard clocks, including in Bugatti cars. By the mid-century Doxa was a respected producer of dress and everyday watches, including the Bauhaus-inspired Grafic line.

In 1967 Doxa launched the SUB 300, developed with input from professional divers and with ties to Jacques-Yves Cousteau's circle. Its orange dial, chosen after tests showed orange was the most legible colour underwater, and its patented unidirectional bezel with a US Navy no-decompression table made it a genuine professional tool. The 1968 SUB 300T Conquistador was among the first dive watches with a helium release valve, and from 1973 novelist Clive Cussler put an orange Doxa on the wrist of his hero Dirk Pitt.

The quartz crisis hit Doxa hard and the brand became part of the Synchron group alongside Cyma and Ernest Borel, with production dwindling through the late 1970s and 1980s. In 1997 the Jenny family, watchmakers for four generations, acquired Doxa and moved its headquarters to Biel/Bienne. Faithful reissues of the SUB 300, SUB 300T and SUB 600T fuelled a revival, and under CEO Jan Edöcs and the Walca Group the brand has expanded internationally with carbon, titanium and GMT variants while keeping prices in the tool-watch sweet spot.

name: Nivada Grenchen
tagline: Revived 1926 Swiss brand behind the Antarctic, Depthmaster and Chronomaster
summary: Nivada Grenchen is a Swiss brand founded in Grenchen in 1926 and revived in 2018 by Guillaume Laidet. Its faithful reissues of mid-century tool watches such as the Chronomaster Aviator Sea Diver, Antarctic and F77 have made it one of the most successful heritage revivals of recent years.
history:
Nivada was founded in 1926 in Grenchen, in the canton of Solothurn, by Otto Wüllimann, Hermann Schindler and Jakob Schneider, and was registered as Nivada AG in 1932. Through the 1950s and 1960s it became a significant exporter, particularly to the United States where it was distributed through Croton. The brand built a reputation for robust, affordable tool watches: the Antarctic of 1950, linked to expeditions to the polar regions; the Chronomaster Aviator Sea Diver chronograph with its distinctive broad-arrow hands and multi-scale bezel; and the 1964 Depthmaster, rated to 1,000 metres at a time when that was exceptional.

Like many mid-sized Swiss firms, Nivada was badly hurt by the quartz crisis of the 1970s and 1980s, and the name faded into the vintage market, where its chronographs and divers became sought-after collectibles.

In 2018 French entrepreneur Guillaume Laidet, who had previously built the William L. 1985 brand, secured the rights to the name through supplier Rémi Chabrat of the Montrichard Group. Rather than raising capital, Laidet funded production through pre-orders. The relaunch began with the Chronomaster, followed by the Depthmaster, Antarctic, Datomaster, Super Antarctic and the integrated-bracelet F77, which became the brand's best seller. Production reached around 6,000 watches in 2023, and Laidet applied the same revival model to Vulcain and Excelsior Park. Nivada Grenchen marks its centenary in 2026.

name: Vulcain
tagline: The Cricket, the mechanical alarm watch of American presidents
summary: Vulcain is a Swiss watchmaker founded in 1858 in La Chaux-de-Fonds and best known for the Cricket, launched in 1947 as one of the first practical mechanical alarm wristwatches. Worn by several US presidents, it has been relaunched since 2021 under Guillaume Laidet's leadership.
history:
Vulcain traces its origins to 1858, when Maurice Ditisheim began making watches in La Chaux-de-Fonds; the Vulcain name was registered in 1894 by the Ditisheim family firm. The company made precision pocket watches and chronographs and exhibited at world's fairs, earning medals for complicated pieces.

Its defining moment came in 1947 with the Cricket, one of the first mechanical alarm wristwatches loud enough to be genuinely useful, thanks to a double membrane and resonance chamber in the caseback. The alarm was likened to a cricket's chirp. In 1953 President Harry Truman received a Cricket, and the watch became associated with the White House, worn or owned by Presidents Eisenhower, Nixon and Lyndon Johnson; the company later branded it 'the watch of presidents'. Vulcain also built the Cricket Nautical of 1961, a dive watch with an alarm designed to warn divers of decompression stops.

The quartz crisis hit Vulcain hard and ownership changed several times, including a period under Swiss watch groups in the 1970s and 1980s. The brand was revived in 2002 and moved to Le Locle, where it continued producing its in-house alarm calibres in small quantities, but it struggled commercially. Around 2021 revival specialist Guillaume Laidet, known for Nivada Grenchen, began working with the Luxembourg-based owners, expanding the watchmaking team and dealer network and relaunching the Cricket Classique, Cricket Tradition and President lines alongside Skindiver and 1970s-style chronographs.

name: Favre-Leuba
tagline: One of Switzerland's oldest watch names, now revived in Le Locle
summary: Favre-Leuba traces its roots to 1737 in Le Locle, making it one of the oldest Swiss watch brands. Known for pioneering mechanical altimeter and depth-gauge watches (the Bivouac and Bathy), it has been relaunched since 2024 under CEO Patrik Hoffmann with backing from Indian retailer Ethos.
history:
Favre-Leuba's story begins in 1737, when Abraham Favre registered as a watchmaker in Le Locle. His descendants built the business over generations, and in 1815 Frédéric Favre partnered with Auguste Leuba, giving the company its lasting name. Favre-Leuba became an early exporter, and from the 19th century it built a strong presence in India, where it remained a household name for generations.

In the 1960s the firm produced a remarkable run of tool watches. The 1962 Bivouac was the first mechanical wristwatch with an aneroid barometer-altimeter, measuring altitude up to 3,000 metres, and the 1968 Bathy included a mechanical depth gauge for divers. The Twin-Power calibre of the same era used two mainspring barrels to extend power reserve, and the Sea King and Sea Chief became popular export models.

The quartz crisis brought decline, and the family sold the brand in the 1980s; it passed through Benedom (LVMH) before Indian conglomerate Tata acquired it in 2011. Tata's 2016–2017 relaunch produced the Raider Harpoon and a modern Bivouac 9000 altimeter watch but was halted after a few years. In 2023–2024 the brand passed to new owners linked to Indian luxury watch retailer Ethos, which put industry veteran Patrik Hoffmann, formerly of Ulysse Nardin, in charge. Relaunched at Geneva Watch Days 2024, Favre-Leuba quickly rolled out Chief, Harpoon Revival and Sky Raider collections, presented its first tourbillon in 2025 and joined Watches and Wonders in 2026. India remains its largest market.

name: Universal Genève
tagline: The Polerouter and Compax maker, reborn under Breitling in 2026
summary: Universal Genève, founded in 1894, was one of the great Swiss chronograph and micro-rotor makers, creator of the Tri-Compax and the Gérald Genta-designed Polerouter. After decades of dormancy it was acquired by Breitling in 2023 and relaunched in April 2026 with a new in-house micro-rotor movement.
history:
Universal was founded in 1894 in Le Locle by Numa-Emile Descombes and Ulysse Georges Perret, and moved to Geneva in 1919, later adopting the name Universal Genève. The firm became a chronograph specialist: in 1917 it made one of the first wristwatch chronographs, in 1936 the Compur, and in 1944 the celebrated Tri-Compax, combining chronograph, triple calendar and moonphase for its 50th anniversary.

In 1954 the young Gérald Genta designed the Polerouter to commemorate Scandinavian Airlines' first commercial flights over the North Pole. From 1955 it was powered by the micro-rotor Microtor calibre, one of the first micro-rotor automatic movements, and the brand later produced the ultra-thin Golden Shadow. The 1960s Compax chronographs gained a cult following, including the 'Nina Rindt' Compax worn by the wife of racing driver Jochen Rindt.

The quartz crisis devastated the company. It changed hands several times, going to Hong Kong's Stelux group in 1977 and later to Hong Kong-based Hong Kong Boom Group in 1989, and output dwindled until the brand went effectively dormant in the 2000s. In late 2023 Breitling, controlled by Partners Group, acquired Universal Genève. After more than two years of development it relaunched on 8 April 2026 as 'Le Couturier de la Montre', with a new Polerouter powered by the UG-110 micro-rotor calibre, a Compax with the micro-rotor chronograph UG-200, the reversible Cabriolet and the Disco Mini, and a return to Geneva's Rue du Rhône.

name: Gallet
tagline: The 1826 chronograph pioneer reborn by Breitling for its bicentenary
summary: Gallet is a historic Swiss chronograph and timer maker founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1826, famous for the 1939 Flying Officer with its world-time bezel and the MultiChron chronographs. Acquired by Breitling, it was relaunched in 2026 as an accessible sister brand with travel- and aviation-themed collections.
history:
Gallet & Co. was established in 1826 by Julien Gallet in La Chaux-de-Fonds, though the Gallet family traces watchmaking roots in Geneva back to the 15th century. Julien's son Léon expanded the business into the United States from the 1850s, and in 1890 his grandson Jules Racine founded Jules Racine & Co. in New York as the exclusive US distributor. After acquiring the Electa watch company in 1907, Gallet grew into one of the leading producers of stopwatches and professional timers; by the 1930s it supplied a large share of the timers used in America, and its timers are associated with timing pioneering aviation, including the Wright Brothers' era.

In 1939 Gallet introduced the Flying Officer, described as the first chronograph wristwatch with a multiple time zone calculator on a rotating bezel. An early example was presented to Senator, later President, Harry S. Truman. The MultiChron family followed, spanning pilot, racing, yachting and waterproof 'clamshell' chronographs, and Gallet was a favourite of military and motorsport users through the 1960s.

The quartz crisis and a shrinking market for mechanical timers reduced the company to a niche player, and it left family ownership in 1994, continuing at small scale under various owners. In 2025 Breitling acquired the name, adding it to a 'house of brands' alongside Universal Genève. Gallet relaunched in 2026, exactly 200 years after its founding, with four collections: the Flying Officer, Multichron Pilot, Multichron Sport and the Gallet Classics, the last powered by Breitling's manufacture B09 calibre. Positioned below Breitling in price, the new Gallet leans on a 'wanderlust' identity rooted in aviation and travel.

name: Enicar
tagline: 'Racine' reversed: the Sherpa tool watches that went to Everest
summary: Enicar was a major Swiss watch manufacturer founded in 1913 by the Racine family, best known for its Sherpa line of compressor-cased divers, chronographs and GMTs. The Swiss company collapsed in the quartz crisis; the name has been owned since 1988 by Hong Kong's Wah Ming Hong and is sold mainly in Asia.
history:
Enicar was founded in 1913 by Ariste Racine, whose family had been watchmakers since the 19th century; the brand name is simply 'Racine' spelled backwards. The company grew into a sizable manufacture based in Lengnau near Biel, producing its own movements and building a strong export network, notably in China where it was distributed from the 1930s by Hong Kong's Wah Ming Hong.

Enicar's golden era came in the 1950s and 1960s. In 1956 a Swiss expedition wore Enicar watches on the first ascent of Lhotse and the second ascent of Everest, and the brand promptly launched the Sherpa line. Sherpa models used EPSA 'Super Compressor' cases with twin crowns and internal rotating bezels, and included the Sherpa Super-Dive, the Sherpa Graph and Super Graph chronographs, the Sherpa Jet and Super Jet GMTs and the Sherpa Date. Enicar promoted its 'Ultrasonic' movement cleaning process and Seapearl waterproof cases, and its chronographs were worn in motorsport, while tennis champion Ken Rosewall wore a Sherpa Date.

The quartz crisis devastated Enicar. After years of losses the Swiss company ceased operations in the late 1980s, and in 1988 Wah Ming Hong acquired the trademark. Under Hong Kong ownership Enicar became one of the best-known imported watch brands in China, selling mainly quartz and Sellita-powered mechanical watches through Asian distribution while advertising itself as 'Enicar of Switzerland'. Outside Asia the brand is known almost entirely through vintage Sherpas, which have become sought-after collector pieces.

name: Edox
tagline: 'The Water Champion' since the 1961 Delfin
summary: Edox is an independent Swiss watchmaker founded in 1884 in Biel and now based in Les Genevez in the Jura. Known for water-resistance innovations like the Delfin and Hydro-Sub, record-thin movements and motorsport chronographs, it produces around 30,000–40,000 watches a year under the Strambini family.
history:
Edox was founded in 1884 in Biel/Bienne by Christian Rüefli-Flury, a watchmaker from Grenchen. The name derives from ancient Greek for the 'measuring of time', and the hourglass logo appeared around 1900. After the founder's death in 1921, Robert Kaufmann-Hug took over and steered production toward wristwatches.

In 1961 Edox launched the Delfin, whose double caseback, special gaskets and double O-ring system gave it outstanding water resistance, earning Edox its 'Water Champion' slogan. The 1965 Hydro-Sub introduced a crown system with tension ring and shock-absorbing gasket rated to 500 metres, and in 1970 the Geoscope offered a world-time display. The brand also built the Chronorally and other racing-inspired chronographs.

The quartz crisis forced Edox to sell its shares to ASUAG, a forerunner of the Swatch Group, in 1973. In 1983 company president Victor Strambini bought back all the shares, making Edox independent again, and relocated it to Les Genevez in the Jura mountains. There it built a reputation for technical feats, notably the Les Bémonts Ultra Slim of 1998 with a 1.4 mm movement, a record thickness the brand still claims. From 2010 Edox became official timekeeper of the World Rally Championship and later the Dakar Rally, and it has partnered with motorsport and powerboat racing. Now led by CEO Alexandre Strambini, the family-owned company makes 30,000–40,000 watches a year, split between Ronda quartz and Sellita-based automatics, sold in more than 60 markets.

name: Fortis
tagline: Grenchen tool watches tested in space since 1994
summary: Fortis is a Grenchen watchmaker founded in 1912 that made the first mass-produced automatic wristwatch with John Harwood in 1926 and supplied Russia's cosmonauts from 1994. Since 2018 owner-CEO Jupp Philipp has rebuilt it around bold Flieger, Marinemaster and Stratoliner tool watches.
history:
Fortis was founded in 1912 by Walter Vogt in Grenchen, in the canton of Solothurn. In 1926 the company worked with British inventor John Harwood to produce the first serially manufactured automatic wristwatch, using Harwood's hammer-style self-winding system, an achievement shown at the Basel fair that year. Fortis introduced chronographs in 1937 and water-resistant models in 1943, and built a line of robust pilot and sport watches through the post-war decades.

Fortis became closely associated with spaceflight. After tests connected with early space programmes, it became from 1994 the supplier of watches for crewed missions authorised by the Russian space agency, and the Official Cosmonauts Chronograph, powered by the Lemania 5100, became standard issue on the Mir and later the International Space Station. Fortis also won the 2004 European Aviation Watch Award and produced notable art editions with painters and designers.

The brand struggled financially in the 2010s and underwent a debt restructuring around 2017. German investor and watch enthusiast Jupp Philipp acquired Fortis, renaming the company Fortis Watches AG and becoming CEO. He reorganised the range into 'Space, Sky and Sea' pillars with in-house-developed WERK calibres built on Swiss ébauches, launching the Flieger F-39/F-41/F-43, the colourful Marinemaster M-40 and M-44 divers, the dust-textured Stratoliner chronographs and the stratospheric-flight-tested Novonaut. The relaunch, featuring the chunky 'Block' bracelet, has made Fortis a favourite among modern tool-watch enthusiasts.

name: Glycine
tagline: Makers of the 1953 Airman, the original pilot's GMT
summary: Glycine is a Swiss brand founded in Biel in 1914, celebrated for the 1953 Airman, a 24-hour pilot's watch that predated the Rolex GMT-Master and was used by US pilots in Vietnam and by astronaut Pete Conrad. Owned by Invicta Watch Group since 2016, it now sells Airman, Combat and Sea Kraken models at accessible prices.
history:
Glycine was founded in 1914 in Biel/Bienne by Eugène Meylan, who named the company after the wisteria flower (glycine in French). Early production focused on small, jewellery-like ladies' watches and innovative miniature movements, and in the 1930s Glycine developed one of the early automatic movements for wristwatches.

The brand's defining moment came in 1953 with the Airman, designed for airline pilots crossing multiple time zones. Its 24-hour dial, rotating 24-hour bezel locked by a crown at 4 o'clock and hacking seconds let pilots read a second time zone, and it reached the market a year before Rolex's GMT-Master. The Airman became standard kit for many US Air Force pilots during the Vietnam War, and in 1965 astronaut Pete Conrad wore one on the Gemini 5 mission.

The quartz crisis weakened Glycine, but it survived as an independent under Hans Hollenstein, who took over in 1984 and kept the Airman alive with new variants such as the Airman 7 and the Airman Base 22, along with Combat military-style watches and the Incursore. In 2016 the company was sold to Invicta Watch Group of Florida, which retained Swiss production while broadening distribution, especially through online retail. Today Glycine's collections include the Airman, the Combat Sub dive watches, the Combat field watches, the Airpilot and the Sea Kraken, sold mostly online at prices well below their official list prices.

name: Squale
tagline: Professional dive watches and case maker to the industry since 1959
summary: Squale (French for 'shark') is a Swiss dive-watch brand founded by Charles von Büren in Neuchâtel, whose cases were once supplied to other famous brands. Owned by the Italian Maggi family since the 1980s and headquartered in Ticino, it is best known for the 50 Atmos 1521 with its crown at 4 o'clock.
history:
Charles and Hélène von Büren established a watchmaking business in Neuchâtel around 1948, specialising in dive watches, and in 1959 registered the Squale trademark along with an early patent for the production of diving watch cases. Squale's case expertise made it a supplier to other brands, and its robust divers found favour with professionals. In 1965 Italian freediver Enzo Maiorca set a world record at 67 metres wearing a Squale Master.

The 1970s were Squale's heyday. The 50 Atmos model reference 1521, with its crown at 4 o'clock and distinctive orange minute hand, became the brand's icon, and Squale became official supplier to the Italian Navy and the Folgore paratroopers brigade. Italy became its most important market, where the Maggi family acted as distributor.

As Charles von Büren prepared for retirement, he sold the brand in 1982 to the Maggi family, who had worked closely with the company. The quartz era was difficult, but in 2005 the Maggis relaunched Squale and restarted production of its classic references, including the 1521, the Squalematic and the 1545. The modern range has broadened with the vintage-sized Sub-39 and Sub-37, the Super-Squale, the T-183 and numerous collaborations. In 2020 Squale moved its headquarters from Milan to Chiasso in Switzerland's Ticino canton, and it sponsors freediver Vincenzo Ferri. Squale remains a favourite among enthusiasts seeking professional-grade Swiss divers at approachable prices.

name: Aquastar
tagline: 1960s dive-instrument pioneer behind the Deepstar and Benthos 500
summary: Aquastar was founded in 1962 by diver-watchmaker Frédéric Robert and built some of the most inventive dive and regatta watches of the 1960s and 1970s, sold through Scubapro and Aqualung. Revived in 2019–2020 under Rick Marei, it reissues the Deepstar chronograph, Benthos 500 and Model 60 from Biel.
history:
Aquastar was established in 1962 by Frédéric Robert, a watchmaker and passionate diver who had taken over the JeanRichard firm and refocused it on functional instruments for aquatic use. Robert filed numerous patents covering crowns, rotating bezels and decompression tables, and Aquastar watches were sold initially through professional diving outlets such as Scubapro and Aqualung rather than jewellers.

The brand's catalogue from the 1960s and 1970s reads like a list of dive-instrument experiments. The Model 60 skin diver of the late 1950s and early 1960s was followed by the Deepstar, a dive chronograph with a no-decompression bezel, and around 1970 by the Benthos 500, a hefty professional diver with a central 60-minute chronograph. Aquastar also became known for regatta timers such as the Regate, with coloured countdown discs for sailing starts, and for the Airstar pilot's chronograph of 1965.

After Robert retired, the Eren Group acquired Aquastar in 1975, and in 1982 the Seinet brothers took over and moved into quartz models. For decades the brand survived mainly as a maker of regatta timing watches while vintage pieces became collector favourites. In 2019 the Synchron Group, under dive-watch revivalist Rick Marei, who had previously been involved in Doxa's reissues, acquired Aquastar and moved it to Bienne. The 2020 Deepstar re-edition was followed by the Deepstar II, the Benthos 500 Founder's Edition with its original central chronograph, the Benthos Heritage and the Model 60 MKII.

name: Luminox
tagline: Always-visible tritium tool watches made for the Navy SEALs
summary: Luminox was founded in California in 1989 by Barry Cohen and became famous for its always-glowing tritium tube illumination and its Navy SEAL watches. Wholly owned by Switzerland's Mondaine Group since 2016, it sells rugged, affordable sea, land and air tool watches in over 30 countries.
history:
Luminox was founded in 1989 by Barry Cohen in the United States with a simple proposition: a watch that could be read in total darkness without first being charged by light. Instead of conventional luminous paint, Luminox used small sealed glass tubes containing tritium gas, whose beta decay makes a phosphor coating glow continuously for many years. The brand called this 'Luminox Light Technology'.

In the early 1990s Luminox developed a watch for the US Navy SEALs, and the Navy SEAL series, particularly the carbon-reinforced 3000 and 3500 families, became the brand's signature. It went on to make branded pieces for units including the US Coast Guard and US Air Force, and partnered with Lockheed Martin on pilot's watches inspired by aircraft such as the F-117 Nighthawk, SR-71 Blackbird, F-16 and F-22. Later partnerships included Bear Grylls survival watches.

Swiss watch maker Mondaine, with which Luminox had long worked on production, acquired a 50% stake in 2006 and became the sole owner in 2016, moving the brand's base to Switzerland and making its watches Swiss made. Today Luminox organises its range into sea, air, land and space collections, including the Navy SEAL, Pacific Diver, Leatherback Sea Turtle, Atacama Field and P-38 Lightning lines, with most pieces powered by Swiss quartz and some by automatic movements, and it supports the Navy SEAL Foundation.

name: Victorinox
tagline: The Swiss Army Knife maker's tough, accessible Swiss watches
summary: Victorinox, founded in 1884 by Karl Elsener and famous for the Swiss Army Knife, entered watches in 1989 under the 'Swiss Army' name. Its watches, led by the ultra-tough I.N.O.X., offer Swiss-made quality at accessible prices and are sold worldwide.
history:
Victorinox began in 1884 when Karl Elsener opened a cutlery workshop in Ibach, in the canton of Schwyz. In 1891 the company began supplying knives to the Swiss Army, and the multi-tool 'Officer's Knife' that followed became the world-famous Swiss Army Knife. The company name, adopted in 1921, combines the name of Elsener's mother Victoria with 'inox', the term for stainless steel.

Victorinox entered the watch business in 1989 in the United States, where watches were sold under the 'Swiss Army' brand through the distributor Swiss Army Brands. The watches, often styled after field and military pieces with a Swiss cross logo, became popular affordable Swiss-made timepieces through the 1990s. In 2001 Victorinox established Victorinox Swiss Army Watch AG and took full control of the watch business in 2002. In 2005 it acquired its long-time rival Wenger, which also had a watch line.

Victorinox watches emphasise durability and value. The I.N.O.X., launched in 2014, was put through more than 100 extreme tests, including being run over by a tank and dropped from height, and became the flagship of the range, later extended in titanium, carbon and mechanical versions. Other collections include the FieldForce, Journey 1884, Alliance and Dive Pro. The company remains controlled by Elsener family foundations and is led by Carl Elsener Jr., with around 90% of its production exported to more than 100 countries.

name: Mondaine
tagline: The Swiss railway clock, shrunk down for the wrist
summary: Mondaine is a family-owned Swiss watch company founded in 1951 by Erwin Bernheim, best known for its Official Swiss Railways watches based on Hans Hilfiker's iconic SBB station clock. The Mondaine Group also owns Luminox.
history:
Mondaine was established in 1951 by Swiss businessman Erwin Bernheim after he took over the Neuchâtel Watch company, originally founded in 1928. For its first decades the company produced affordable watches for other brands and private labels, benefiting from the rise of quartz technology.

The turning point came in 1986, when Mondaine obtained the commercial licence from the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) to use the design of the Swiss railway clock. Created in 1944 by SBB engineer Hans Hilfiker, the clock face with its bold black batons and red 'lollipop' seconds hand is a design icon that appears in museums worldwide. Mondaine's Official Swiss Railways watches translated the design to the wrist and became the brand's signature. The station clocks famously sweep the seconds hand round in 58 seconds and pause at 12 for about two seconds while awaiting a central signal; in 2013 Mondaine launched the stop2go, whose movement recreates that stop at 12.

In 2012 Apple used the railway clock design in iOS 6, leading to a licensing agreement between SBB and Apple. Mondaine has broadened its line-up with the evo2, the Simply Elegant, the Helvetica range inspired by the typeface, the automatic 'Original' and the sustainable 'essence' line using bio-sourced materials. The group became sole owner of Luminox in 2016 and also holds watch licences such as Pierre Cardin. It remains owned by the Bernheim family.

name: Swatch
tagline: The plastic 'second watch' that saved Swiss watchmaking
summary: Swatch launched in 1983 as a low-cost, 51-part plastic quartz watch that revived the Swiss industry after the quartz crisis and became a global pop-culture phenomenon. The flagship brand of the Swatch Group, it scored another sensation in 2022 with the Omega x Swatch MoonSwatch.
history:
By the early 1980s the Swiss watch industry had been devastated by cheap Japanese and Hong Kong quartz watches. At ETA, part of the struggling ASUAG group, managing director Ernst Thomke tasked engineers Elmar Mock and Jacques Müller with creating a radically cheap Swiss watch. Their design used just 51 parts, a plastic case into which the movement was directly built, and ultrasonically welded construction that made it impossible to repair but cheap to mass-produce. The name was a contraction of 'second watch'.

The first twelve Swatch models were launched on 1 March 1983 in Zurich at around 50 Swiss francs. Backed by bold marketing and a fashion-driven approach of new seasonal collections, Swatch became an instant hit, and Nicolas G. Hayek, who engineered the merger of ASUAG and SSIH into SMH (renamed the Swatch Group in 1998), made it the engine of the Swiss recovery. Artist collaborations with Keith Haring, Kiki Picasso and others, the Pop Swatch, Chrono, Scuba, Irony metal watches and the ultra-thin Skin kept the brand in the spotlight, and Swatch collecting became a craze.

In 2013 the brand launched the Sistem51, the first mechanical movement with fully automated assembly, again using just 51 parts. In 2020 Swatch introduced bio-sourced plastics, then bioceramic. The March 2022 Omega x Swatch MoonSwatch, a bioceramic take on the Speedmaster, caused queues around the world, and in 2023 the Blancpain x Swatch Scuba Fifty Fathoms followed. Swatch remains headquartered in Biel/Bienne, with Nick Hayek Jr. leading the group.

history:
Hanowa was founded in 1963 in Biel/Bienne by Hans Noll and his wife Elisabeth Wirz, two years after Noll had taken over the sales management of a watch factory in the town. The company name was formed from the first letters of the founder's name, HAns NOll, and 'WAtch'. Hanowa built a business producing affordable Swiss watches for international distribution, and survived the quartz era by embracing quartz movements and value pricing.

In 1990 the company launched a second brand, Swiss Military Hanowa, drawing on the values associated with the Swiss armed forces: robustness, endurance and reliability. The brand's watches carry the Swiss cross, and since 2015 Hanowa has been an official licensee of the Swiss Confederation, allowing it to market products under the 'Swiss Military' name. The company later moved its headquarters from Biel to Möhlin in the canton of Aargau.

Swiss Military Hanowa's catalogue is large and varied, from simple quartz watches such as the Flagship Heritage to chronographs, ceramic-bezel sports pieces like the Sidewinder, aviation-themed Avia models and automatic divers including the Maître Plongeur. Positioned well below mainstream Swiss mid-range brands, it sells through department stores, military exchanges and online retailers across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, and it marked its 60th anniversary in 2023.

name: Traser
tagline: Swiss tritium-lit tactical watches born from a US Army contract
summary: Traser is the watch brand of mb-microtec, the Bern-area specialist in self-powered tritium light sources (trigalight). Created in 1989 to build a watch robust enough for the US Army, it makes affordable Swiss-made tactical, outdoor and dive watches readable in total darkness.
history:
Traser is the watch brand of mb-microtec ag, a company based in Niederwangen near Bern that specialises in gaseous tritium light sources, tiny sealed glass capsules whose inner phosphor coating glows continuously thanks to the beta decay of tritium gas. The company markets this technology as 'trigalight', and it is used in instruments, gun sights and signage as well as in watches.

The traser watch brand was established in 1989 to meet a specific military requirement: a watch tough enough for the US Army that could be read at night without any external light or charging. The resulting P6500 Type 6 was issued to US forces and became one of the first self-illuminating military watches, establishing traser's reputation among soldiers, law enforcement and outdoor professionals. For a time traser also produced watches for other brands using its light sources.

Over the following decades traser built a broad range of Swiss-made watches organised into tactical, outdoor and diver collections, all built around trigalight tubes on the hands and indices, which remain visible for up to 20 years. Popular models include the P67 Officer Pro, P65 Tactical Mission, P68 Pathfinder with solar and automatic variants, the lightweight P99 Tactical Carbon and professional divers with helium valves and ceramic bezels rated to 500 metres. traser remains part of mb-microtec, positioning itself as a practical, affordable Swiss alternative for users who need guaranteed night-time legibility.

name: Formex
tagline: Biel independent with a patented shock-absorbing case suspension
summary: Formex is a family-owned independent watchmaker founded in Biel in 1999, known for its patented Case Suspension System that cushions the movement from shocks. Its Essence, Reef and Field models offer COSC-certified Swiss automatics at aggressive prices, and it now makes its own micro-rotor calibre.
history:
Formex was founded in 1999 in Biel/Bienne, initially building a reputation for sporty, design-led watches, including chronographs with motorsport themes, and for manufacturing expertise it also offered to other brands. The company is family-owned and has always emphasised in-house design and engineering over heritage storytelling.

Formex's signature innovation is its patented Case Suspension System, in which the inner case holding the movement is mounted on a shock-absorbing suspension within an outer structure. The system protects the movement from impacts while letting the watch sit comfortably and flex slightly with wrist movement. Formex also developed quick-release straps and bracelets, micro-adjustable carbon-fibre clasps and tool-free interchangeable bezels.

The brand's modern breakthrough came in 2019 with the Essence, launched with a strong direct-to-consumer approach and offering a COSC-certified chronometer, sapphire crystal, ceramic or carbon options and the suspension case at a price rarely seen for Swiss chronometers. It was followed by the Reef dive watch with 300 m water resistance and swappable bezels, the lightweight Essence Leggera, the titanium Field Automatic, the Stratos UTC and the Essence ThirtyNine. name: Ernest Borel
tagline: The 'dancing couple' brand and its kaleidoscope Cocktail watch
summary: Ernest Borel is a Swiss watchmaker founded in Neuchâtel in 1856 by Jules Borel, known for its dancing-couple logo and the kaleidoscopic Cocktail watch of the 1950s. Owned by Chinese investors since the late 1990s, it is a major Swiss brand in China and other Asian markets.
history:
Ernest Borel was founded in 1856 in Neuchâtel by Jules Borel, working with his brother-in-law Paul Courvoisier. The young company built a reputation for precision: it won first place at the Neuchâtel observatory chronometry competition in 1866 and took awards at the 1876 Philadelphia and 1878 Paris exhibitions. The business passed to Jules's son Ernest Borel, whose name it carries.

In the 1950s the brand created one of its most distinctive designs, the Cocktail watch, whose dial pattern appears to shift like a kaleidoscope as the wearer moves the wrist. It became an emblem of the brand in Asia, alongside the logo of a dancing couple that signifies romance and togetherness. Ernest Borel had been distributed in China and Hong Kong since the early 20th century and became a well-known Swiss name there.

The Borel family ran the company until 1975, when, during the quartz crisis, it joined the Synchron group with Doxa and Cyma. In 1997 Chinese investors bought the brand, which was later listed in Hong Kong as Ernest Borel Holdings, and in 2018 Hong Kong-based Citychamp Watch & Jewellery Group acquired a controlling interest. Now based in Le Noirmont in the Jura, Ernest Borel focuses on traditionally styled automatic and quartz watches for men and women, including the Cocktail, Retro, Heartful and Sage collections, with most of its sales in Greater China and Southeast Asia.

name: Perrelet
tagline: Named for the inventor of the self-winding watch, famed for the Turbine
summary: Perrelet honours Abraham-Louis Perrelet, the Le Locle watchmaker credited with inventing the self-winding mechanism around 1777. Revived in 1995 and owned by Spain's Festina Group since 2004, the Biel-based brand is best known for its Double Rotor and spinning-blade Turbine watches.
history:
Abraham-Louis Perrelet (1728–1826) was a watchmaker from Le Locle who, around 1777, developed a self-winding mechanism using an oscillating weight set in motion by the wearer's walking. The Geneva Society of Arts reported that about fifteen minutes of walking would wind the watch for eight days. His invention influenced Abraham-Louis Breguet, who developed his own 'perpétuelle' self-winding watches, and Perrelet is widely credited as the father of the automatic watch.

The modern Perrelet brand was established in 1995 in his honour. Its first signature product, the Double Rotor, placed a visible rotating weight on the dial side synchronised with the conventional rotor on the back, making the automatic winding itself part of the display. In 2004 the brand was acquired by the Spanish Festina Group, which also owns Candino and Jaguar, and it is based in Biel/Bienne.

In 2009 Perrelet introduced the Turbine, whose dial is covered by a set of titanium blades, inspired by jet engines, that spin freely with the motion of the wrist to reveal the dial beneath. The Turbine became the brand's bestseller and spawned many variations, from the Turbine Toxic to Turbine Pilot and Diver versions. Perrelet also produced complications priced well into six figures, the Lab Peripheral with its peripheral rotor, and in 2021 the P-331-MH in-house calibre with COSC certification. The brand produces around 30,000 watches a year.

name: Graham
tagline: Left-handed Chronofighter trigger chronographs honouring George Graham
summary: Graham is a La Chaux-de-Fonds-based chronograph specialist founded in 1995 in homage to George Graham, the 18th-century London master who worked on early timing mechanisms. It is best known for the Chronofighter, with its oversized left-side trigger inspired by WWII RAF pilots' chronographs.
history:
The brand takes its name from George Graham (c.1673–1751), the English clock and instrument maker who apprenticed under Thomas Tompion, married his niece and succeeded him. Graham introduced the deadbeat escapement in precision regulators and invented the mercury pendulum, built early orreries and astronomical instruments for Greenwich, mentored Thomas Mudge and gave an interest-free loan to John Harrison. He is also credited by the brand with pioneering early timing devices that anticipate the chronograph. He is buried in Westminster Abbey alongside Tompion.

The modern Graham brand was established in 1995 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, adopting 1695, the year George Graham joined Tompion's workshop, as its heritage date. From the outset it focused on chronographs, and in 2001 it launched the Chronofighter, whose large lever-operated trigger on the left side of the case was inspired by devices used by British bomber pilots during World War II, allowing the chronograph to be started and stopped with a thumb even while wearing gloves.

The Chronofighter became the brand's identity, evolving into Oversize, Vintage, Superlight carbon and skeleton versions. Graham also created the Swordfish, with magnifying 'big eye' lenses over the subdials, the Silverstone motorsport chronographs, and the Geo.Graham Tourbillon Orrery, a haute horlogerie tribute to Graham's astronomical work. Graham sells largely direct and through selected retailers, with Chronofighter Vintage models forming its core range in 2026, the 25th anniversary of the Chronofighter.

name: Arnold & Son
tagline: Astronomy, chronometry and world time in homage to John Arnold
summary: Arnold & Son is a high-end manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds named after John Arnold, the 18th-century English chronometer pioneer who coined the modern use of the term 'chronometer'. Part of the Citizen group through movement maker La Joux-Perret, it is known for the giant-moon Luna Magna, Perpetual Moon, Globetrotter and Time Pyramid.
history:
John Arnold (1736–1799), born in Bodmin, Cornwall, was among the most important English watchmakers of the 18th century. Working in London from around 1762, he designed practical, accurate marine chronometers that could be made in quantity from about 1782, gave the word 'chronometer' its modern meaning and invented the overcoil balance spring still used in most mechanical watches. His chronometer 'Arnold 36' performed remarkably in trials at the Royal Observatory. In 1787 he founded Arnold & Son with his son John Roger Arnold, supplying chronometers to the Royal Navy and explorers, and he formed a close friendship with Abraham-Louis Breguet, who trained John Roger.

The name was revived in 1995 as a Swiss brand within The British Masters group, which also launched Graham. In 2010 it became part of the La Joux-Perret movement manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds, and in 2012 Japan's Citizen group acquired the holding company, giving Arnold & Son access to substantial in-house movement development.

Arnold & Son organises its work around three pillars: astronomy, chronometry and world time. Its astronomical watches include the Perpetual Moon, with a large hand-painted moon accurate for 122 years, and the Luna Magna, featuring a three-dimensional half-marble, half-aventurine moon. Chronometry is represented by the Time Pyramid with its vertically stacked skeleton movement, the Nebula, the Ultrathin Tourbillon and constant-force designs, while the Globetrotter displays world time with a sculpted Northern Hemisphere dome. All are powered by manufacture calibres.

name: Angelus
tagline: Le Locle's chronograph-calendar pioneer, revived as a high-end manufacture
summary: Angelus was founded in Le Locle in 1891 by the Stolz brothers and became celebrated for complicated chronographs such as the 1942 Chronodato and the Datalarm alarm watch. Revived in 2015 by movement maker La Joux-Perret, part of the Citizen group, it now makes avant-garde tourbillons and vintage-inspired chronographs.
history:
Angelus was founded in 1891 in Le Locle by brothers Gustav and Albert Stolz, and developed into one of the most innovative movement-making manufactures of the first half of the 20th century. The firm specialised in complications, producing chronographs, alarm watches, travel clocks and repeaters, and supplied movements to other brands.

In 1942 Angelus launched the Chronodato, one of the first serially produced wristwatch chronographs with a full calendar, followed by chronographs with triple calendar and moon phase. In the 1950s it introduced the Datalarm, an alarm wristwatch with date, and the Tempomatic automatic. Angelus's small, beautifully made desk and travel clocks, including eight-day and alarm models, were also widely admired. Like many of its peers, the company was hit hard by the quartz crisis, and the brand fell dormant in the 1970s.

In 2011 the Angelus name was acquired by La Joux-Perret, the La Chaux-de-Fonds movement maker owned since 2012 by Japan's Citizen group. After several years of development, the brand was relaunched in 2015 with the U10 Tourbillon Lumière, followed by skeleton tourbillons, a tourbillon diver, rattrapante tourbillons and a modern Chronodate with a sapphire-framed movement. More recently Angelus has balanced its avant-garde L.A.B. line with the La Fabrique collection of vintage-inspired chronographs such as the Instrument de Vitesse and the Chronographe Télémètre, all powered by in-house calibres designed, produced, finished and tested in-house.

name: Louis Erard
tagline: Regulator dials and cult collaborations from Le Noirmont
summary: Louis Erard is a Swiss watchmaker founded in 1929 and based in Le Noirmont in the Jura, known for regulator-dial watches. Under CEO Manuel Emch it has become a darling of collectors through limited collaborations with Alain Silberstein, Vianney Halter, Konstantin Chaykin and others at accessible prices.
history:
Louis Erard was founded in 1929 in La Chaux-de-Fonds by Louis Erard and André Perret, producing watches in the Jura watchmaking tradition. The company later settled in Le Noirmont in the Franches-Montagnes, where it remains. For decades it was a modest, family-run producer of classic mechanical watches.

The company changed hands in 1992 for family reasons, and in 2003 it was acquired by a group of investors led by Alain Spinedi, who repositioned Louis Erard as a mid-range Swiss brand offering traditional mechanical watches, notably its Excellence and Heritage lines, at competitive prices. The regulator layout, in which the hours, minutes and seconds are shown on separate axes, became a signature of the house.

In 2019 Manuel Emch, formerly of Jaquet Droz and Romain Jerome, took the helm and reinvented the brand around limited-edition collaborations. The Le Régulateur Louis Erard x Alain Silberstein of 2020, with its playful coloured hands and geometric shapes, sold out rapidly, and was followed by partnerships with independent watchmakers Vianney Halter and Konstantin Chaykin, artist Monica Bonvicini and pop-culture names such as Astro Boy, as well as Métiers d'art editions featuring grand feu enamel, marquetry and hand engraving. Grouped into the Noirmont X, Noirmont Métiers d'art, 2340 and Hall of Fame lines, Louis Erard now offers creative independent-style watches at a small fraction of typical independent prices.

tagline: Young, family-owned Swiss sports brand with Kenissi manufacture movements
summary: Norqain is an independent, family-owned Swiss brand founded in 2018 by Ben Küffer and based in Nidau near Biel. It makes adventure-themed sports watches, including the Adventure, Freedom 60, Independence and the ultralight Wild ONE, many powered by manufacture calibres made with Kenissi.
history:
Norqain was founded in 2018 by Ben Küffer, who grew up in a watch-industry family. Founding partners included former NHL player Mark Streit and Ted Schneider, whose family had long owned Breitling.

Norqain launched with the Adventure line, sturdy sports watches in steel and bronze with a distinctive textured 'Norqain plate' personalisation on the side of the case, and the Freedom 60, a vintage-inspired chronograph. A key strategic step came when the brand secured manufacture calibres from Kenissi, the movement maker associated with Tudor, powering models such as the Independence and Adventure Neverest with chronometer-certified automatics and 70-hour power reserves.

In 2022 Norqain introduced the Wild ONE, with a case made of NORTEQ, a lightweight carbon composite, and an integrated shock-absorbing rubber structure, designed to be extremely light and robust. Skeletonised versions and a Wild ONE Skeleton Chrono followed. The brand has built partnerships in ice hockey, including with the NHL, and with Swiss national sports teams and adventure ambassadors. Still independent and family-owned, Norqain has grown rapidly into one of Switzerland's most successful new watch brands. Its growth has been built on a direct relationship with retailers and a deliberately broad line-up spanning steel, bronze, gold and composite cases.

name: Bell & Ross
tagline: Square cockpit-instrument watches from a Paris-Swiss house
summary: Bell & Ross was founded in Paris in 1992 by Bruno Belamich and Carlos Rosillo, and is famous for the BR 01 and BR 03 square watches modelled on aircraft cockpit instruments. history:
Bell & Ross was founded in 1992 in Paris by two friends, designer Bruno Belamich and businessman Carlos Rosillo, whose nicknames 'Bell' and 'Ross' give the brand its name. The project began as a university idea to create professional instrument watches for pilots, divers and other specialists. In its early years the watches were produced by Sinn in Frankfurt, a respected maker of tool watches, and Bell & Ross gained credibility with professionals including bomb-disposal and military units.

Chanel acquired a minority stake in the company, and in 2002 production moved from Germany to Switzerland, with a manufacturing base in La Chaux-de-Fonds while design and headquarters remained in Paris. In 1998 the Hydromax 11100M set a Guinness World Record for water resistance, rated to 11,100 metres thanks to its oil-filled case.

The brand's breakthrough came in 2005 with the BR 01, a large square case with a round dial directly inspired by aircraft cockpit instruments. The design became one of the most recognisable of the 2000s and spawned the smaller BR 03, as well as the round Vintage and BR V2 lines. Bell & Ross has supplied watches to French Air Force squadrons and partnered in Formula 1 with Renault and later the Alpine F1 Team. In 2019 it launched the BR 05, an integrated-bracelet 'urban' sports watch, followed by the BR-X5 with a manufacture calibre developed with Kenissi, and in 2023 a redesigned 41 mm BR 03.

name: Zodiac
tagline: Sea Wolf dive watches since 1953, now under Fossil
summary: Zodiac was founded in Le Locle in 1882 by Ariste Calame and is best known for the 1953 Sea Wolf, one of the first purpose-built dive watches, and the colourful Super Sea Wolf. Owned by Fossil Group since 2001, it has faced uncertainty after Fossil's 2025 restructuring, though Fossil named it one of its core brands.
history:
Zodiac was established in 1882 in Le Locle by Ariste Calame; the Zodiac name was registered in 1908, and Calame's son Louis Ariste Calame took over in 1895 after attending watchmaking school. In 1930 the company introduced the Autographic, a self-winding watch with power-reserve indicator, unbreakable crystal and radium dial.

In 1953 Zodiac launched the Sea Wolf, one of the first purpose-built dive watches for the consumer market, appearing in the same year as the Blancpain Fifty Fathoms and Rolex Submariner. The 1960 Aerospace GMT extended the design to air travel, and in the late 1960s the Astrographic displayed time with 'floating' hands on transparent discs. The early-1970s Super Sea Wolf, with a larger case rated for greater depths, was supplied to the US Navy SEALs and other military users, and its bright dials and bezels made it a 1970s icon.

The quartz crisis brought Zodiac to its knees and it changed hands several times before Fossil acquired it in 2001 for about $4.7 million. Fossil used Zodiac as its Swiss-made mechanical brand, with watches powered by movements from Fossil's STP subsidiary, and relaunched the Sea Wolf and Super Sea Wolf in 2015 with vintage-inspired designs, followed by colourful limited editions, the Olympos and the Aerospace GMT. In October 2025 Fossil Group filed for Chapter 15 protection as part of a restructuring, and heavy discounting followed, but Fossil identified Zodiac, alongside Skagen and Relic, as a core brand it intends to keep.

history:
Delma's story began in 1924, when brothers Adolf and Albert Gilomen founded A. & A. Gilomen S.A. in Lengnau, near Biel. One of the company's original models was named Delma, and the name soon became the brand itself. In 1946 the firm introduced its first chronograph, the Midland, in 18k yellow gold.

In 1966 the company was taken over by Ulrich Wüthrich and partners and renamed Delma Watch Ltd. Under Wüthrich, Delma moved decisively into sports and dive watches: the Periscope arrived in 1969, followed in the 1970s by the Shell Star and Quattro professional divers, whose rugged designs found favour with divers and collectors alike. The distinctive Shark model, with its rectangular case, debuted in 1981, and Delma survived the quartz era by combining mechanical and quartz production and maintaining broad international distribution.

In the 21st century Delma has concentrated on its diving heritage. The Blue Shark line, introduced in 2011, evolved through several generations with ever-greater water resistance, culminating in the 47 mm Blue Shark IV rated to 5,000 metres, one of the most water-resistant production watches available. Alongside it, Delma offers reissues and modern versions of the Shell Star, Quattro, Periscope, Commodore, Cayman and Santiago. Now led by the second and third generations of the Wüthrich family, Delma remains fully independent after a century in business, celebrating its centenary in 2024.
